```{r, message = FALSE}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(grf)
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)
library(viridis)

# Load the balanced panel (798,756 rows)
final_model_data <- read_csv("../../data/cleaned/model_data_final.csv",
                             show_col_types = FALSE)

# Clean up memory 
gc()
```

## Model Construction
```{r}
set.seed(123)

model_sample <- final_model_data

# Prepare Matrices 
# We include Weather to 'soak up' the noise from rain/snow accidents
Y <- as.numeric(model_sample$y_count)
W <- as.numeric(model_sample$treatment)
X <- model_sample %>% 
     select(baseline_risk, y_coord, dist_60th, week_index, avg_temp, tot_precip) %>% 
     as.matrix

# Check for NA's before training
message("NAs in X: ", sum(is.na(X)))
message("NAs in Y: ", sum(is.na(Y)))
message("NAs in W: ", sum(is.na(W)))

X <- scale(X)

# Ensure treatment is binary
table(W)


# HARDWARE & ALGORITHM OPTIMIZATION

# Detect M4 Pro cores and leave 1 free so macOS doesn't freeze
cores <- detectCores() - 1 
message("Utilizing ", cores, " cores for parallel processing...")

# Percent of model_sample we will use for modeling
smpl_frac <- 1.00


# TRAIN THE LLCF 
# Train Propensity Model (W.hat)
message("[", Sys.time(), "] Training Nuisance Model: W.hat")
w_forest <- regression_forest(
  X, W,
  num.trees = 500,
  clusters = model_sample$hex_id,
  sample.fraction = smpl_frac,
  tune.parameters = "all", # Optimizes for the 97:3 imbalance
  num.threads = cores,     # Enables parallel processing
  seed = 123
)
W_hat <- w_forest$predictions

# Train Outcome Model (Y.hat)
message("[", Sys.time(), "] Training Nuisance Model: Y.hat")
y_forest <- regression_forest(
  X, Y,
  num.trees = 500,
  clusters = model_sample$hex_id,
  sample.fraction = smpl_frac,
  tune.parameters = "all", 
  num.threads = cores,     # Enables parallel processing
  seed = 123
)
Y_hat <- y_forest$predictions

# Train Causal Forest
message("[", Sys.time(), "] Training Causal Forest")
cf_final <- causal_forest(
  X, Y, W,
  W.hat = W_hat,
  Y.hat = Y_hat,
  num.trees = 500,
  clusters = model_sample$hex_id,
  sample.fraction = smpl_frac,
  tune.parameters = "all", 
  honesty = TRUE,
  num.threads = cores,     # Enables parallel processing
  seed = 123
)

# How "comparable" is our control group?
hist(W_hat, breaks = 50, main = "Propensity Score Overlap")

# Calculate Global Results
ate <- average_treatment_effect(cf_final, target.sample = "treated")
message("Average Treatment Effect (ATE): ", round(ate[1], 4), " (SE: ", round(ate[2], 4), ")")

# Test for Heterogeneity - The Signal check
test_calibration(cf_final)
```

# Spatial Prediction
```{r}
# Create and Clean the Prediction Grid
post_treatment_weeks <- model_sample$week_index[model_sample$treatment == 1]
target_week <- median(post_treatment_weeks)

X_map_df <- model_sample %>%
  distinct(hex_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(week_index = target_week) %>%
  # Global averages for the target week to fill any potential holes
  mutate(
    avg_temp = mean(model_sample$avg_temp[model_sample$week_index == target_week], na.rm=TRUE),
    tot_precip = mean(model_sample$tot_precip[model_sample$week_index == target_week], na.rm=TRUE)
  )

# Force Impute any remaining NAs
# If a hex had NA weather for the whole target week, the mean() above might be NA
X_map_df <- X_map_df %>%
  mutate(
    avg_temp = if_else(is.na(avg_temp), mean(model_sample$avg_temp, na.rm=TRUE), avg_temp),
    tot_precip = if_else(is.na(tot_precip), 0, tot_precip)
  )

# Generate Matrix
X_map_mat <- X_map_df %>%
  select(baseline_risk, y_coord, dist_60th, week_index, avg_temp, tot_precip) %>%
  as.matrix()

# Final NA Check - This should print 0
message("NAs found in prediction matrix: ", sum(is.na(X_map_mat)))

# Scale and Predict
x_center <- attr(X, "scaled:center")
x_scale  <- attr(X, "scaled:scale")

X_map_scaled <- scale(X_map_mat, center = x_center, scale = x_scale)

predictions_map <- predict(cf_final, 
                           newdata = X_map_scaled,
                           linear.correction.variables = c(2, 3), 
                           estimate.variance = TRUE)

# Re-calculate treatment status for the prediction dataframe
# Since this is a post-treatment map, 'treatment' is just 'in_zone'
X_map_df <- X_map_df %>%
  mutate(
    treatment = in_zone, 
    cate = as.numeric(predictions_map$predictions),
    se = sqrt(as.numeric(predictions_map$variance.estimates))
  )

# Filter to the CBD (Treatment Zone)
map_data <- X_map_df %>% filter(treatment == 1)

# How many hexes did we catch?
message("Number of treated hexes in map: ", nrow(map_data))

# Check the spread
if(nrow(map_data) > 0) {
  print(summary(map_data$cate))
} else {
  message("Warning: Still no treated units. Check if 'in_zone' exists in X_map_df.")
}

# Join to your hex_grid sf object
map_sf <- hex_grid %>%
  inner_join(map_data, by = "hex_id")

ggplot(map_sf) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = cate), color = "white", size = 0.05) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(
    low = "blue", 
    mid = "white", 
    high = "red", 
    midpoint = 0,
    name = "CATE\n(Collisions/Week)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Heterogeneous Impact of Congestion Pricing on Collisions",
    subtitle = "Conditional Average Treatment Effects (CATE) by Hexagon",
    caption = "Red = Increase, Blue = Decrease. Estimates include Local Linear Correction."
  )
```

```{r}
did_model <- lm(y_count ~ post * in_zone + avg_temp + tot_precip, data = final_model_data)
summary(did_model)
```
